items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Charlie and I became very good friends.

ctx.x: So I didn't know all this -- what they talk about now, that discrimination stuff. I didn't experience -- because I was a professional man, and in the professional business, there's no discrimination. We don't have that. So we finished the show down there, and of course, I was a little older then. And I could get around more than when I was with Honey Potter.

And I associated and I met plenty of people, and there was Ed Small. He was boss of -- he owned Small's Paradise. Charlie Johnson was in there, had the band for years. Charlie and I became very good friends. I used to go in there, and one time there was a showgirl that I took up there once, and some gangster up there, Jerry Preston, he was after her or something like that. And somebody said that she was in there, going to Small's Paradise with Scottie, the trumpet player. We just went in there one night, there…

And Jerry made a remark that I'm coming after him. And it came to me. And Ed Small heard about it. He's the boss. Well, he sent word to me that -- come on in there whenever you want, Scottie, Jerry ain't coming after anybody. And I knew all the fellows in the band, in Charlie Johnson's band. And I could have played in his band, but I was working.
